archetype: high-end urban condominium tower or stepped mid-rise with a legible resident lobby, secure vertical circulation, differentiated luxury dwelling plans, balconies or terraces, shared amenity space, service infrastructure and a gravity-coherent partial structural failure story
ground_program: formal street-facing resident entrance with weather protection, vestibule and staffed or formerly staffed lobby rather than a direct opening into private dwelling space
secure transition from lobby to elevator/stair core with mail, parcel, reception or concierge functions positioned along the public-to-private threshold
separate service/loading entrance connected to refuse, maintenance, utility and freight circulation without routing deliveries through the principal lobby
ground-floor amenity or management spaces such as resident lounge, fitness room, office, storage or building services arranged around real circulation and exterior access
parking, loading or lower service zones are present only where supported by the footprint and grade, with credible ramps, stairs or doors rather than sealed decorative voids
principal structural bays, shear walls, columns and core geometry remain legible enough to support the upper massing and to make later damage physically interpretable
street setback, planters, drop-off apron, retaining walls, drainage and foundation edges seat the building into terrain without a monolithic artificial podium
corner conditions react to surrounding streets or open space with differentiated glazing, entrances, amenity frontage or service placement rather than repeating one facade on every side
upper_program: multiple condominium units per occupied floor with individually legible entrances from common circulation and coherent living, kitchen, sleeping, sanitation and storage zones
larger corner or premium units use additional exposure, balconies, terraces or expanded living space so luxury status is expressed through plan and circulation rather than palette alone

at least one vertically continuous enclosed stair core with supported landings, uninterrupted player headroom and destinations on every occupied level; larger footprints should retain a second independent egress core
elevator shafts, if represented, remain vertically aligned and terminate in real lobby, machine, service or penthouse zones rather than floating or stopping arbitrarily
common corridors remain short, secure and legible, with unit doors opening from shared circulation and no route passing through neighboring residences
balconies and terraces are supported by slabs, walls, brackets or structural edges and connect to actual occupied rooms through usable doors
mechanical, electrical, water and rooftop plant spaces are grouped around credible service risers and maintenance routes rather than scattered as decorative machinery
roofline, penthouse, terrace and mechanical massing create a distinct upscale residential silhouette without collapsing into a featureless rectangular cap
circulation: residents move from street entrance through lobby and secure common circulation to individual units without crossing loading, refuse or utility spaces
service staff can move from loading or service entry to freight/service circulation, utility rooms and refuse areas without passing through private residences
every occupied level retains a continuous player-scale route to at least one supported stair core and an exterior exit direction
premium amenities, roof terraces or penthouse spaces are reachable only through real resident or service circulation and not by decorative inaccessible shafts
unit interiors preserve coherent circulation from entry to living, sleeping, sanitation and balcony/terrace spaces without impossible overlaps or one-block choke points
damage variants must preserve at least one complete lobby-to-unit route and one viable vertical egress path through a surviving portion of the building
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a luxury condominium building with surviving units, common circulation and amenity/service zoning rather than a generic ruined tower shell

favor localized facade peel, balcony failure, fire spread, shattered glazing, partial floor collapse, burst utilities, water damage and one major structural breach over repeated rectangular deletion masks
a major shattered section may expose several stacked units, but surviving slab edges, columns, shear walls, core walls and debris must tell one gravity-coherent failure story
where floors or balconies fail, associated partitions, doors, furnishings, glazing and service lines must fail consistently so unsupported fragments do not float
preserve enough intact premium dwellings, lobby elements, balconies or terraces and amenity/service rooms for upscale residential identity to remain inferable
at least one stair core must remain physically continuous through the surviving occupied portion; a second core may be severed only where the damage story clearly supports it
service risers, elevator shafts and mechanical spaces may be exposed by damage but must remain vertically aligned and structurally related to the surviving core
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the structure reads immediately as an upscale multi-unit condominium rather than a generic apartment block, hotel or office tower
resident lobby, secure common circulation, dwelling units, amenities, service/loading functions and rooftop or mechanical spaces form a believable building program
premium units differ meaningfully through plan, exposure, balconies, terraces or room scale rather than simple material substitution
stairs are vertically supported, land on real floors and provide continuous player-scale headroom to every surviving occupied level
balconies, terraces, glazing and facade openings correspond to real occupied rooms and remain structurally supported where intact
the shattered section exposes coherent stacked residential anatomy and gravity-driven damage rather than arbitrary missing cubes
at least one complete lobby-to-unit route and one viable vertical egress route survive the damage state
the building meets street, setback, loading and grade conditions without floating foundations, buried entrances or a rectangular artificial platform
